articles.headline: Fantasy football Week 6 inactives: Hurts, Jackson ruled out; Flowers to play
articles.description: Updated inactives and analysis based on the latest reports and official announcements leading up to kickoff.
articles.headlineJa: ファンタジー・フットボール第6週の欠場選手情報：ハーツとジャクソンは欠場、フラワーズは出場へ
articles.descriptionJa: キックオフ前の最新レポートと公式発表に基づく、最新の欠場選手情報と分析。
articles.body:
Whom should you start? Whom should you sit? To help you set your fantasy football lineups and avoid starting an offensive player who won't be in the lineup, we'll post fantasy-relevant updates and analysis here as NFL teams release their official inactives lists. 

Official Sunday inactives should begin coming in approximately 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff times: around 11:30 a.m. ET for the early games and 2:30 p.m. ET for the late-afternoon games.

Refresh often for the latest information.

Don't forget to check these out: Mike Clay's Playbook | Week 6 Buzz 

Week 6 Rankings | Matchup rankings for Week 6

Biggest concerns ahead of Sunday

Players with early starts

Michael Penix Jr, QB, Falcons (ribs): Penix has been a full participant at practice all week long. He has been removed from the injury report and will start Sunday. Penix has yet to throw multiple TD passes or score 15 fantasy points in any game this season. He is purely for use in superflex formats, but his availability is great for Bijan Robinson and Drake London. Both are elite options with Penix under center.

Zay Flowers, WR, Ravens (toe): Flowers was added to the team's injury report Thursday but is not on the final report, meaning he will play in Week 6. His production took a hit without Jackson last week, but Flowers still saw nine targets in that game from QB Tyler Huntley, who will be under center again this week. Volume should keep him in play as a WR2. It's also worth noting that Rashod Bateman missed practice this week due to a shoulder injury but is also not on the final injury report, so he will play too. Rookie WR Ja'Kobi Lane is practicing in full and Jeremy Fowler reports he is "good to go" for Week 6. He is worth stashing if you have a bench spot available.

Caleb Williams, QB, Bears (hamstring): Williams has been a full participant at practice and is questionable in Week 6. He might opt to run less initially, but Williams is still in play as a QB1. I would use him over Trevor Lawrence, Jameis Winston and Jacoby Brissett. However, I would go with either Kirk Cousins or Jordan Love over Williams.

Quinshon Judkins, RB, Browns (ankle): Judkins missed practice to start the week before getting in a limited session Friday. He is questionable and his status truly seems to be up in the air for Week 6. If he sits, the Browns will be left with Jaleel McLaughlin and Audric Estime on the active roster. McLaughlin is the preferred play and, while the floor is low, he'd be in the flex conversation due to volume. It's also worth noting that Dylan Sampson had his 21-day window for return opened this week, but he is out for Week 6.

KC Concepcion, WR, Browns (concussion): Concepcion has cleared the league's concussion protocol and will play in Week 6. Though we have seen flashes, Concepcion is more of an upside depth stash for now. Fantasy managers should instead go with some of the other streaming WR options listed in this article.

articles.headline: Commanders RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt out vs. 49ers with groin injury
articles.description: Commanders running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt won't play against the 49ers because of a groin injury, coach Dan Quinn said.
articles.headlineJa: コマンダーズのRBジャコリー・クロスキー＝メリット、鼠径部の負傷により49ers戦を欠場
articles.descriptionJa: ダン・クイン監督によると、コマンダーズのランニングバック、ジャコリー・クロスキー＝メリットは鼠径部の負傷により49ers戦には出場しない。
articles.body:
ASHBURN, Va., -- Washington Commanders running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt won't play Monday against the San Francisco 49ers because of a groin injury, coach Dan Quinn said Saturday.

Croskey-Merritt did not practice all week because of the injury, which he had been dealing with entering Sunday's 27-27 tie against the visiting New York Giants in Week 5. He managed 11 carries for 82 yards but had just one carry after the third quarter.

He missed the final two preseason games because of a groin injury. Quinn called the latest setback a reinjury.

Croskey-Merritt leads Washington with 239 rushing yards and two touchdowns.

Without him, the Commanders will rely on Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler. White has been dealing with a shoulder issue that caused him to be limited Friday after being a full participant a day earlier. Ekeler, who signed before Week 4, has been limited in practice with a chest issue.

Jeremy McNichols will travel with the team to San Francisco and could be activated off injured reserve ahead of Monday's game. McNichols started the season on IR because of a quad injury suffered this summer.

Quinn did not say if wide receiver Stefon Diggs would play after he missed the Giants game with a hamstring injury. Diggs was limited in practice Friday. If he plays, it would be the first time, Diggs, wide receiver Terry McLaurin and quarterback Jayden Daniels have been on the field together since Week 2.

It's also possible the Commanders will return cornerback Trey Amos and safety Nick Cross. Amos has been on injured reserve because of an ankle injury, but he and Cross, who hasn't played since Week 2 with an internal injury, were full participants in practice.

articles.body:
We are back with more European soccer this weekend!

We kicked things off at the Hill-Dickinson Stadium as Chelsea put in a solid performance and earned a 2-0 win over Everton.

Later, Brentford hosted Liverpool, as the Reds looked to build on their midweek UEFA Champions League win against LASK and Andoni Iraola's side did that with a 2-1 comeback win.

Elsewhere across the continent, Bologna welcome Inter Milan in Serie A, while Real Betis face unbeaten Barcelona in LaLiga. Over in the Bundesliga, Union Berlin took on contenders Borussia Dortmund as the match ended in a scoreless draw, while defending champions Bayern Munich host RB Leipzig.

articles.headline: USMNT's Gio Reyna scores in Strasbourg's defeat to PSG
articles.description: Ousmane Dembele inspired a Paris St Germain comeback after coming off the bench to score and contribute an assist in their 3-1 victory at Strasbourg in Ligue 1.
articles.headlineJa: USMNTのジオ・レイナ、ストラスブールのPSG戦でゴール
articles.descriptionJa: ウスマヌ・デンベレが途中出場から得点とアシストを記録し、パリ・サンジェルマンの逆転劇を牽引。リーグ・アンのストラスブール戦を3-1で勝利に導いた。
articles.body:
United States international Giovanni Reyna scored in Strasbourg's 3-1 Ligue 1 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain on Saturday. 

Ousmane Dembélé inspired a PSG comeback after coming off the bench to score and contribute an assist.

It was an overhauled line-up for Luis Enrique, who initially rested most of his regular starters with the game falling in between Wednesday's brilliant win at Manchester City and Tuesday's Champions League meeting with Barcelona.

Reyna's 17th-minute opener remained the only goal after Dembélé missed with a 72nd-minute penalty.

He made up for it first by teeing up Illia Zabarnyi's equaliser, then firing PSG in front for the first time with five minutes remaining before Désiré Doué added a stoppage-time third.

None of Achraf Hakimi, Nuno Mendes, Willian Pacho, Fabián Ruiz, Vitinha, Dembélé or Doué started, though most were later introduced as second-half substitutes.

The hosts took the lead with one of their earliest opportunities. Genesis Antwi won the ball and found Gessime Yassine, who slipped a pass to Reyna.

The USMNT attacker, who was sandwiched between two white shirts, unleashed an effort that appeared to take a slight deflection before crossing the line.

Matvei Safonov was able to prevent Strasbourg from quickly doubling their lead when he saved an Oso effort seven minutes later.

- Raphinha due back for Barça vs. Betis; Flick will manage PSG, Madrid minutes

- Man City's alternate universe: Guardiola, Haaland to Arsenal? Arteta to PSG?

Lucas Beraldo fired wide for PSG on the half hour, and Strasbourg goalkeeper Filip Jorgensen was called into action to deny Dro Fernández with nine minutes remaining in the first half.

Pape Diop then directed an effort towards Safonov but it was too weak to truly trouble the PSG keeper, who made a straightforward save to prevent any further damage before the break.

There was a shot to open the second half from Conrad Harder, who tried again with a header three minutes later, saved by Safonov.

Enrique reinforced his side, introducing Vitinha, Doué, Mendes, Hakimi and Dembélé by the 65th minute, but the threat continued to come from Strasbourg as Gessime Yassine, Harder, Soumaila Coulibaly and Jeyland Mitchell called Safonov back into action.

Dembélé then squandered a golden chance to draw the sides level after Diop was charged with a handball, stepping up to take the resulting penalty only to send it wide.

He somewhat made up for the mistake when, five minutes later, he delivered the perfect cross and Zabarnyi applied the finish from point-blank range.

Redemption was complete after the hosts failed to nod away a cross, and the ball fell favourably for the Ballon d'Or winner, who wove his way through a crowd before firing PSG in front.

Doué then added a stoppage time cushion, tucking in the visitors' third from an incisive Torres pass.

articles.headline: Premier League VAR review: Should Brentford's Yarmoliuk have been sent off vs. Liverpool?
articles.description: VAR often causes controversy, but how are decisions made? Our resident ref, Andy Davies, explains all.
articles.headlineJa: プレミアリーグVAR検証：ブレントフォードのヤルモリウクはリヴァプール戦で退場になるべきだったか？
articles.descriptionJa: VARはしばしば物議を醸すが、判定はどのように下されるのか？専門レフェリーのアンディ・デイビスが詳しく解説する。
articles.body:
The video assistant referee causes controversy every week, whether it be the Premier League, Champions League or FA Cup, but how are those decisions made and are they correct?

For the 2026-27 season, we are taking a look at the major incidents to explain the process in terms of both VAR protocol and the laws of the game. The most surprising, controversial and complicated decisions will be examined all season long right here.

 Andy Davies (@andydaviesref) is a former Select Group referee, with over 12 seasons on the elite list, working across the Premier League and Championship. With extensive experience at the elite level, he has operated within the VAR space in the Premier League and offers a unique insight into the processes, rationale and protocols that are delivered on a matchday. 

Should Brentford's Yarmoliuk have been sent off?

Brentford 1-2 Liverpool (Oct. 17)

Referee: John Brooks

VAR: Darren England

Time: 45 + 3 minutes

Incident: Brentford defender Yehor Yarmoliuk sent off for violent conduct.

What happened: With Liverpool setting up for a corner kick and time ticking away at the end of the first half, Brentford defender Yarmoliuk and Liverpool's Jérémy Jacquet clashed, with the Liverpool player ending up on the floor.

Following a lengthy VAR review, referee Brooks agreed with the VAR recommendation and finally sent Yarmoliuk off for committing a violent action and headbutting Jacquet.

VAR decision: VAR overturn. Red Card for violent conduct.

VAR review: England took time to recommend an on-field review, as Yarmoliuk's violent action wasn't conclusive from all replay angles. However, the penalty-area tight camera eventually gave him the clear evidence he needed to ask John Brooks to visit the pitch-side monitor and review the incident.

Verdict and insight: A correct VAR intervention in this incident, with Brentford's Yarmoliuk committing a violent action towards his opponent and the red card an expected outcome.

Like Rodrigo Bentancur's red card for Spurs in the last match round, when a player deliberately heads at an opponent and makes contact, it is very likely to end in a red card.

The four minutes it took VAR to reach the point of an on-field review is frustrating, as this should have been cleared up a lot quicker -- this will be something ProRef will need to improve moving forward.

Additionally, some discussion as to why the restart was not a penalty kick, considering it was a defender committing an offense on an attacker in the penalty area. However, the ball was not in play when the incident occurred and therefore the original corner restart was correct.

VAR: Paul Howard

Time: 62 minutes

articles.headline: Erling Haaland brace helps Man City hold off Ipswich at defiant Etihad Stadium
articles.description: Erling Haaland struck twice as defiant Manchester City marched on at the top of the Premier League by holding on for a 3-2 win over Ipswich.
articles.headlineJa: ハーランドの2得点でマン・シティが粘り、エティハド・スタジアムでイプスウィッチを退ける
articles.descriptionJa: アーリング・ハーランドが2ゴールを決め、マンチェスター・シティはイプスウィッチを3-2で下して、プレミアリーグ首位を快走した。
articles.body:
Erling Haaland struck twice as defiant Manchester City marched on at the top of the Premier League by holding on for a 3-2 win over Ipswich.

Phil Foden was also on target at the Etihad Stadium but City needed to survive a nervy finish after a Zian Flemming penalty gave the visitors late hope.

It was City's second successive league victory since the club were found guilty of serious breaches of the competition's financial regulations last month.

It also maintained their 100% start to the campaign under new manager Enzo Maresca and lifted them six points clear of champions Arsenal at the top of the table.

Promoted Ipswich rallied to cancel out Foden's opener through Daizen Maeda but Haaland's double, taking his tally for the campaign to 12 in all competitions, looked to have reasserted City's authority.

The Norwegian was denied a hat trick by VAR, and the game ended in frantic fashion, but City had done enough.

 

The stands were awash with inflatable bananas throughout as City's supporters continued to show their backing for the club during their ongoing crisis.

The blow-up fruit -- a throwback to a craze from the 1980s and '90s -- has quickly come to symbolise their defiance and the team have also remained unfazed.

City captain Rúben Dias forced an early save from Christian Walton but the Ipswich goalkeeper could not prevent Foden giving the hosts the lead on 19 minutes.

Jérémy Doku cut inside the from the left and pulled back for Foden who, in his first appearance since his red card at Old Trafford last month, turned home from eight yards.

City's lead lasted just two minutes as Abdoul Ouattara released Maeda with a well-weighted ball down the right.

The pass arced around the backtracking Marc Guéhi and Maeda outpaced and the outmuscled the England centre-back to seize possession and sit Gianluigi Donnarumma down with a composed finish.

Emersonn missed the target from another Ipswich attack but City regained their lead on 34 minutes when Mateo Kovacic reached the byline and pulled back for Haaland to power a header through Walton's grasp.

Dias then forced another save from Walton while Haaland, Iliman Ndiaye and Doku all had shots blocked in a strong finish to the first half.

Nico O'Reilly went close after the restart with a header from a corner but Haaland made no mistake to grab his second on 69 minutes.

Ndiaye created the opportunity with a strong run from deep before playing in the striker with a defence-splitting pass. Ouattara could not keep his footing as Haaland skipped past him and coolly beat Walton.

Haaland thought he had claimed a hat-trick and put the game beyond doubt when he volleyed home after an Ndiaye shot had hit the bar, but his strike was disallowed by VAR for offside against Enzo Fernández.

articles.headline: James, Embiid play 76ers' preseason finale, 'still working on our rhythm'
articles.description: Without VJ Edgecombe, who was held out of Friday night's 125-120 loss to the Celtics, 76ers coach Nick Nurse gave the closest glimpse of what his team may look like this season, including LeBron James and Joel Embiid playing preseason highs in minutes.
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- As the 76ers begin a season with a star-laden roster, center Joel Embiid rejects the narrative that anyone needs to sacrifice for this team to succeed.

"I'm against the concept of sacrificing," Embiid said after Friday's preseason finale. "I think the way I explained it was you do what you do best, and we're going to support you. ... I don't think anybody has to take a back seat."

Albeit without second-year starting guard VJ Edgecombe, who was held out of Friday's 125-120 loss to the Boston Celtics for precautionary reasons, Sixers coach Nick Nurse gave the closest glimpse of what his team may look like this season.

The other active Sixers starters -- LeBron James, Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown and Embiid -- all played preseason highs in minutes and well into the second half. Embiid, who struggled in his last appearance two games ago against the Brooklyn Nets, finishing with six points and eight turnovers, was dominant.​

He scored 27 points, grabbed eight rebounds and added five assists. In the third quarter, he had one of the game's highlights when he threw down an emphatic dunk that drew roars from fans at Xfinity Mobile Arena.

"It's good to dunk. I thought I would never dunk again," Embiid said with a smile. "I guess I don't know what happened. I kind of got possessed."

Still, the group never looked comfortable together on the floor, despite playing against Celtics reserves. After the game, players didn't shy away from their somewhat disjointed performance. Brown pointed to the team's spacing Friday night, which he said led to turnovers, as one of the many things they need to fix moving forward.

"We're not where we want to be yet," he said. "So that's just a part of it. It's a part of coming together, a new group with a bunch of guys, different style, but we just got to keep getting better every day."

James echoed Brown's comments, but neither seemed concerned about the Sixers' ability to eventually jell.

"We're getting there," James said. "I mean, obviously we are a couple of weeks in, so we're still working on our rhythm, working on our kinks, and it's not going to be perfect."

The Sixers open the regular season against the New York Knicks on Tuesday.

articles.headline: No. 1 pick AJ Dybantsa injures ankle during Wizards' preseason finale
articles.description: First overall pick AJ Dybantsa exited the Wizards' preseason finale after injuring his ankle on an awkward landing and will undergo further evaluation.
articles.body:
First overall pick AJ Dybantsa exited the Washington Wizards' preseason finale Friday after injuring his ankle on an awkward landing and will undergo further evaluation.

Wizards coach Brian Keefe told sideline reporter Chase Hughes that Dybantsa had suffered a mild ankle sprain but that the decision to keep him out for the rest of the game was more precautionary.

"We'll look at it more when we get more information," Keefe said.

Dybantsa fell to the ground after landing on his left ankle following a midrange jump shot before limping to the locker room. He had scored 12 points in 15 minutes before his exit in the second quarter.

The Wizards open the regular season Wednesday against the Milwaukee Bucks.

articles.headlineJa: ベン・シモンズの「E60」ドキュメンタリーの視聴方法
articles.descriptionJa: 「Being Ben」が日曜日に初放送されます。
articles.body:
Former No. 1 NBA draft pick Ben Simmons sheds light on his polarizing career in a new ESPN E60 documentary, 'Being Ben.' Now with the Sacramento Kings, the documentary explores the ups and downs of his time in the league and the lifelong passion he has for fishing.

Here's more information about the program.

When does it air?

'Being Ben' premieres on Sunday at 4 p.m. ET on ESPN.

How can fans watch?

Following its linear premiere, 'Being Ben' will stream afterward on the ESPN App. It can be watched on the documentary's streaming hub.
